newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Workers Party says will not back PRI.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Workers Party says will not back PRI.

text.p: Mexico's Workers Party (PT), which won a tiny proportion of seats in the lower house of Congress in July 6 elections, will not back the ruling PRI to give it a working majority, its leader said on Monday.

"I assure you, once and for all, in the next legislature we are not going to throw in our cards with the PRI because we've never done that," PT president Alberto Anaya told the weekly news magazine Proceso.

The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party won 239 votes in the lower house elections, losing the majority it has held unbroken since 1929. The PT won six seats and the ecologist PVEM won eight. Analysts had speculated that the PRI would use its considerable muscle to force the two parties to back it.

But Anaya's comments appeared to scotch that possibility. PT officials on Monday also told Reuters the party was planning to work with opposition forces to overturn the government's tax policy as one of its main legislative priorities. It was not immediately clear if the PVEM would back the PRI, but some of its candidates are firmly opposed to the ruling party. The leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution and the conservative National Action Party, which won the bulk of opposition seats in the lower house, are also staunch PRI opponents.
